title: Homogeneous coordinates for continuous cochains with topological coefficients
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $J$ a topological group, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $J$-action. Let $B^n(J,V)$ consist of the jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ satisfying $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ for every $a\in J$, with pointwise $E$-vector space structure and differential
$$(\delta F)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n+1})=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_{n+1}).$$
Let $C^n(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$, $C^0(J,V)=V$, with differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{n}(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
including $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. These are ordinary complexes of abstract $E$-vector spaces, extended by zero in negative degrees. In the derived category $D(E\text{-Vect})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a natural isomorphism $Q(B^\bullet(J,V))\simeq Q(C^\bullet(J,V))$, represented by an actual $E$-linear cochain isomorphism $\Phi:B^\bullet(J,V)\to C^\bullet(J,V)$ with inverse $\Psi$, given by
$$(\Phi_nF)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n),$$
$$(\Psi_nf)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=x_0 f(x_0^{-1}x_1,x_1^{-1}x_2,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n).$$
Thus $\Phi_{n+1}\delta=d\Phi_n$ and $\Psi_{n+1}d=\delta\Psi_n$; in degree zero $\Phi_0F=F(1)$ and $\Psi_0v(x)=xv$. Both cochain isomorphisms commute with continuous equivariant $E$-linear coefficient maps and with restriction along continuous homomorphisms of topological groups (using the restricted action on $V$). No compactness, discreteness, completeness, or local compactness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Pointwise addition and scalar multiplication preserve continuity and equivariance, since addition and scalar multiplication in the topological vector space are continuous and the action is E-linear. Thus each B^n is an E-vector subspace of all functions on J^{n+1}; the same argument gives the pointwise vector space C^n. Here E is a field in the sense of [def-weil-field]. Each coordinate omission is continuous and commutes with simultaneous left multiplication, so the finite alternating sum defining δ maps B^n into B^{n+1} and is E-linear.

proof.text: The homogeneous differential squares to zero by pairwise cancellation. For each pair of original positions 0≤i<j≤n+2, deleting i first and then position j−1 has coefficient (−1)^{i+j−1}; deleting j first and then i has coefficient (−1)^{j+i}. These two terms evaluate F on the identical tuple and sum to zero. Every term in δδF occurs in exactly one such pair. This proves δ²=0 without any assertion about resolutions.

proof.text: Write P_n(g)=(p_0,...,p_n), with p_0=1 and p_i=g_1⋯g_i. Each p_i is continuous: p_0 is constant and p_{i+1}=p_i g_{i+1}, so induction uses continuous multiplication and coordinate projections. Hence P_n is continuous for the finite product topology. Define Φ_n(F)=F∘P_n. It is continuous and E-linear in F. For n=0, the domain J^0 is a point and this is Φ_0(F)=F(1) in V.

proof.text: For a tuple x=(x_0,...,x_n) set r_i=x_{i−1}^{−1}x_i for 1≤i≤n. Each r_i is continuous by continuous inversion and multiplication. Thus x↦(x_0,f(r_1,...,r_n)) is continuous, and the assumed jointly continuous action makes Ψ_n(f)(x)=x_0 f(r_1,...,r_n) continuous. Moreover (ax_{i−1})^{−1}(ax_i)=r_i and (ax_0)w=a(x_0w), proving equivariance. E-linearity of the action proves E-linearity of Ψ_n. The empty-ratio case gives Ψ_0(v)(x_0)=x_0v.

proof.text: At x=P_n(g), one has x_0=1 and x_{i−1}^{−1}x_i=p_{i−1}^{−1}(p_{i−1}g_i)=g_i. Substitution into Ψ gives (Φ_nΨ_nf)(g)=1 f(g_1,...,g_n)=f(g). This includes n=0 and proves Φ_nΨ_n=id by equality of functions.

proof.text: Conversely, the cumulative products of r_i=x_{i−1}^{−1}x_i telescope: r_1⋯r_i=x_0^{−1}x_i. Therefore P_n(r)=(x_0^{−1}x_0,...,x_0^{−1}x_n). Equivariance of F gives (Ψ_nΦ_nF)(x)=x_0 F(x_0^{−1}x_0,...,x_0^{−1}x_n)=F(x). This also holds for the single-coordinate tuple when n=0. Thus Ψ_nΦ_n=id; Φ_n and Ψ_n are inverse E-linear maps.

proof.text: Fix n≥0, F∈B^n and g=(g_1,...,g_{n+1}), and evaluate δF at P_{n+1}(g)=(1,p_1,...,p_{n+1}). Its omission of position 0 is F(p_1,...,p_{n+1}). This tuple equals g_1 times (1,g_2,g_2g_3,...,g_2⋯g_{n+1}); hence equivariance identifies the term with g_1(Φ_nF)(g_2,...,g_{n+1}). Its sign is +1. For n=0 this reads F(g_1)=g_1F(1).

proof.text: For an internal position 1≤i≤n, omitting p_i from (1,p_1,...,p_{n+1}) is exactly the cumulative-product tuple of (g_1,...,g_ig_{i+1},...,g_{n+1}): the cumulative products up to i−1 are unchanged, the next is p_{i−1}(g_ig_{i+1})=p_{i+1}, and the later ones are unchanged. Its sign is (−1)^i. Omitting the final position leaves P_n(g_1,...,g_n), with sign (−1)^{n+1}. Adding these terms and the first omission of Step 7 gives Φ_{n+1}δF=dΦ_nF. For n=0 there are no internal positions and this gives (dv)(g)=gv−v.

proof.text: The displayed d is well-defined and E-linear: its first term uses the jointly continuous action composed with continuous coordinate projections and f; each other term is a continuous f composed with a continuous multiplication/projection map; the sum is finite. Steps 5–8 give d=Φ_{n+1}δΨ_n. It follows that d²=Φ_{n+2}δ(Ψ_{n+1}Φ_{n+1})δΨ_n=0 by Step 2. Thus C is indeed a cochain complex. Also Ψ_{n+1}d=Ψ_{n+1}Φ_{n+1}δΨ_n=δΨ_n. Extending both maps by the unique map on zero spaces in negative degrees gives inverse E-linear cochain maps Φ and Ψ, including the zero differential from degree −1.

proof.text: Let u:V→W be a continuous equivariant E-linear coefficient map. Postcomposition defines maps on both kinds of cochains. It commutes with δ by linearity, and with d because u(gv)=gu(v). Evaluation gives Φ_n(u∘F)=u∘Φ_n(F). For the inverse formula u(x_0 f(r))=x_0 u(f(r)), so Ψ_n(u∘f)=u∘Ψ_n(f). These are equalities of the specified continuous functions, proving coefficient naturality for both cochain isomorphisms.

proof.text: For a continuous homomorphism h:H→J, use the H-action a·v=h(a)·v. Homogeneous restriction is F↦F∘h^{n+1}; inhomogeneous restriction is f↦f∘h^n. They preserve continuity and commute with the differentials: omission commutes with h coordinatewise, and h(ab)=h(a)h(b) identifies every internal product and the action term. Since h(1)=1, h(g_1⋯g_i)=h(g_1)⋯h(g_i), and h(a^{−1}b)=h(a)^{−1}h(b), direct substitution gives Φ_H∘res_B=res_C∘Φ_J and Ψ_H∘res_C=res_B∘Ψ_J. The restricted action is jointly continuous by composition with h×id.

proof.text: Use the localization functor Q of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on the abstract E-vector-space complexes of Step 9. Functoriality gives Q(Ψ)Q(Φ)=Q(ΨΦ)=Q(id_B)=id_{Q(B)} and Q(Φ)Q(Ψ)=id_{Q(C)}. Thus Q(Φ) with inverse Q(Ψ) is the asserted isomorphism in D(E-Vect), represented by the actual cochain isomorphism already constructed. Applying Q to the equalities in Steps 10–11 proves the same naturality in the derived category. Only functoriality is used here, so no topological vector-space derived category or exponential law is involved.
